wholeCurrentGoal.title: Kp und Kc verknüpfen
wholeCurrentGoal.description: Die lernende Person kann den Zusammenhang zwischen Kp und Kc aus der Zustandsgleichung idealer Gase herleiten, beide Konstanten mit passenden Einheiten umrechnen und die Gültigkeitsgrenzen des Modells begründen.
wholeCurrentGoal.descriptionEn: The learner can derive the relationship between Kp and Kc from the ideal-gas equation, convert between the constants using consistent units, and justify the validity limits of the model.

resourceLinkCandidate.title: Visualisierung: Kp und Kc verknüpfen
resourceLinkCandidate.description: Schematisches ideales Gasmodell bei gleicher Temperatur: pᵢ = cᵢRT führt zur Beziehung der unnormierten Druck- und Konzentrationsprodukte. Die symbolische Gasreaktion A₂(g) ⇌ 2 A(g) erläutert Δν als dimensionslose Differenz der gasförmigen stöchiometrischen Koeffizienten. Die Stoffknoten sind keine Molekülstrukturen oder gemessene Gleichgewichtsprobe.
resourceLinkCandidate.altText: Ein schematischer Gasbehälter steht neben pᵢ = cᵢRT und Kp = Kc · (RT)^Δν. Sichtbar sind „Ideale Gase · gleiches T“ und „Unnormierte Produkte“. Darunter zeigt ein blauer A₂-Stoffknoten mit Doppelpfeil auf zwei getrennte gelbe A-Stoffknoten; die eigene Textzeile lautet A₂(g) ⇌ 2 A(g). Rechts stehen „Gas-Koeffizienten“ und Δν = 2 − 1 = 1. Die Stoffknoten sind schematisch und bilden keine Molekülstrukturen ab.

ownConcretePixelNotes.evidence: Both whole DE/EN descriptions require derivation, unit-consistent conversion and ideal-model limits. The image is an orientation map: p_i=c_i RT leads to Kp=Kc(RT)^Delta-nu; the visible ideal-gas/same-T and unnormalised-products labels correctly restrict that displayed relation. It supplies no worked learner performance or experiment.

The lower left contains one connected two-lobed A2 species, the lower middle exactly two separate A circles. Both the pictorial arrows and A2(g) equilibrium 2 A(g) text are reversible; atom counts are 2 on each side. Blue/yellow distinguish displayed species, and A labels identify the conserved element; no atomic-element colour key is asserted.
The right-hand panel says gas coefficients and displays Delta-nu=2-1=1. These are stoichiometric coefficients, not measured gas quantities or units. All participating species are visibly marked (g).

The individual relation p_i=c_i RT is valid with pressure, molar concentration, R and absolute T in consistent units. The displayed Kp=Kc(RT)^Delta-nu is explicitly labelled unnormalised products, so it does not assert the same naked RT factor for standard-state-normalised dimensionless constants. R units and the standard-state factor belong in the actual whole lesson/context, which is pending the subsequent metadata/context pass.

The large visible banner states ideal gases and the same T. It supports comparison/conversion at the same absolute temperature, without claiming that K is temperature-independent or that the ideal model works at arbitrary pressure.

No person uses an instrument or reads a reversed page. The gauge is a generic unnumbered pressure icon; the flask balls are a generic mixed-gas icon without a composition/count assertion. The arrow goes from the individual gas relation to the equilibrium relation. No quantitative vessel volume, pressure reading or experimental result is claimed.

All three actual bound views were individually viewed. At 360 px, the main equations, ideal-gas/same-T condition, unnormalised-products qualifier, gas-coefficient label and A2(g) equilibrium 2 A(g) / Delta-nu=2-1=1 are legible. The 680 px rendering is clear; no clipping, overlap or broken subscripts/exponent is visible.

The actual 1672x941 PNG is approximately 16:9. Thick dark outlines, coloured rounded panels and large abstract particles form an approachable comic-like orientation image. No exceptional format or cropping is needed.
